op.description: The operation to perform: `exec` runs `cmd`, `ping` and `info` are health checks, and `shutdown` ends the session. Callers of the tool do not set this — run_terminal_command always sends `exec`.

cmd.description: The shell command to run, as a single string. It is passed to `sh -c`, so pipes, redirection, globs, quoting, and `&&` all work.

cwd.description: Directory to run this command in. Defaults to the session's current directory, which carries over from earlier calls.

env.description: Environment variables for this command only. A guest-side `export` does not carry over to the next call; this does not either.

stdin.description: Bytes to feed to the command's standard input, base64-encoded.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the command after this many milliseconds. The whole process group is killed and `timed_out` is set on the response. 0 means no timeout.

max_output.description: Cap stdout and stderr at this many bytes each. Output past the cap is dropped and `truncated` is set on the response. 0 uses the session default.
